subject: Transportation Systems
title: Underwater Pressure and Leaks
description: A 60-second lesson on Underwater Pressure and Leaks.

hook.text: Every underwater tunnel fights constant water pressure trying to crush or flood it.

buildup.text: Waterproof linings, drainage systems, and pressure relief valves work together to keep tunnels dry.

discovery.text: Small leaks are normal and expected. Pumps run continuously, removing thousands of gallons per day.

twist.text: During construction, pressurized air was once used to hold water back—causing deadly decompression sickness.

climax.text: Modern waterproofing membranes and segmental concrete linings have made tunnel flooding extremely rare.

punchline.text: Every underwater tunnel leaks. Pumps just work faster.

quiz.question: How do underwater tunnels handle normal water seepage?
